overall_structure.value: Solution-treated structure of the Al-12 low-density steel after 1100 °C/2 h + water quenching. No dedicated EBSD/TEM characterization was reported for the 1100 °C condition; the paper states that increasing the solution-treatment temperature increases the grain size relative to the 1050 °C treatment, which is invoked to explain the slight yield-strength decrease.

unmapped_findings: Sample corresponds to the Al-12 member of the Fe30Mn(x)Al1C series; measured chemical composition (Table 1): C 1.02, Mn 30.47, Al 12.04, Fe Bal. (mass%), with measured density 6.52 g/cm3.

The 1100 °C/2 h + water-quenching treatment was applied to specimens with different Al content specifically to assess the effect of solution temperature; the behaviour for this condition is reported only qualitatively (Fig. 2d, Al-content series at 1100 °C; Fig. 8d, work-hardening rate), with no tabulated numerical strength/elongation values given for the 12%Al / 1100 °C case.

It is reported for the Al-bearing steels that increasing the solution-treatment temperature to 1100 °C produces a slight decrease in yield strength compared with 1050 °C, attributed to an increase of grain size with increasing solution temperature.

For the 12%Al steel after 1100 °C solution treatment, the work-hardening rate is among the lowest of the Al series and the true stress-strain curves extend to noticeably larger true strain (some terminating beyond 0.5) than after 1050 °C (Fig. 8d).

No microstructural (EBSD/TEM) or Charpy impact-toughness data are reported for the 1100 °C solution-treated condition; all tabulated Table 3 microstructure parameters and Table 2 tensile/impact values correspond to the 1050 °C/2 h solution treatment and therefore describe a different (1050 °C) sibling sample.
The overall density of these low-density steels is described by ρ = 8.10 − 0.102C − 0.10Al − 0.01Mn (with C, Al and Mn in mass%), derived from the C, Mn and Al alloy series (Fig. 6b, Eq. 3).
